_readme: The queue of decisions waiting on a named human, rendered by etc/status-board.mjs as its first pane.
This is a QUEUE, not a record: a decision is recorded in its owning document (CLAUDE.md §4), and each entry here points at that document by file + anchor string.
The generator re-reads every anchor at generation time and flags the entry STALE if the anchor is gone, so an entry cannot outlive the sentence it points at without being noticed.

`verify` is an optional shell command; while its output matches `pendingWhen` the entry is live, otherwise the generator reports it RESOLVED and it should be deleted in the next edit. EMPTY output (command failed, gh not authenticated, grep -c exiting 1 on zero) means UNVERIFIED and the entry stays live — a check must never retire an entry by failing.
`ref` (optional) reads the anchor at a git ref instead of the working tree — for decisions posed on a branch that has not landed.
Retire an entry by deleting it in the same PR that records the ruling. Do not leave answered entries here to rot.

When the generated page is published as a Claude artifact with the `db` capability, every live entry carries a ruling widget (accept / modify / reject / defer / question + notes). Those marks are stored in the artifact's database, collection `board-rulings`, one document per entry keyed by the entry's slug (see `slug()` in etc/status-board.mjs) — an INTAKE, not the record: the GM reads them back (Artifact read_db) and writes each ruling into the owning document, in the marker's words, in the same change that acts on it.

decisions.ask: REWRITTEN 2026-09-17 from every-each's list (outbox/20260916T212814Z-every-residue-after-wave.md, every line checked against the spec on #412's tip). LANDED BY THE WAVE (#411 + #412, unstable 083dc8b4): R-T3 the blame set (§6.1) · R-Q7A/B/C the anchored `WITHIN … OF THE JOIN | THE DEADLINE | THE ARMING | <instant>` (§5.1.1) · §5.2 the LEST clock (missed deadline / violating stamp / state deadline; stream trim; re-offer-to-every-layer with the stalled-chain refusal) · AFTER/BEFORE with R-X5 AMENDED (bare `AFTER d1 WITHIN d2` re-anchors; two-offset is `WITHIN d2 OF THE JOIN`) and R-X6 (early act = reported nullity; the `notes` channel) · the Pile-of-Law window-phrase evidence card · EXACTLY swept per #407. OWED, build tracks in the order every-each would cut them, all from post-#412 unstable: (1) Track 5 (+3): the count and measure joins — `ONCE SOME m OF … HAVE` / `AT LEAST m OF` / `ANY OF` (§2.2.7.4; SOME is a keyword, the join is not built), measure joins, §13.2 partial-completion visibility, and the residual of an unfinished barrier carrying its join line (§11.1 BarrierRuntime as a real value — today a resumed residual would run the members and never the join); consumer lts-diagrams-2; the n=0 triple as witnesses. (2) The performer/actor agreement check per member (checkDeonton's comment says phase 2 does it at run time; the machine checks the EVENT's party, not the ACTION's actor). (3) A front-end fix the run time compensates for: a barrier's HENCE/LEST naming the member is refused at run time; the right fix is checkDeonton dropping the variable from scope under a JoinOnce. (4) T1 (§5.1.2.1): no COMMENCING keyword, no separation of the instant sorts — a run-time refusal of a DATE below DATE_SERIAL (YMD 1 1 1) stands in; with it a join-line AFTER, backward windows from a future event, a negative AFTER offset. (5) §5.1.3 the anchor slot as a trace expression — direction only; needs Meng's marks on B1, B3–B9. (6) WHOSE (R-W1–R-W3) — parked by Meng 'until we resolve the WITHIN / AFTER', which is now resolved; type of the expression still open; EACH matched by spelling, NO/WHOSE not keywords, ALL/NO semantics open since 2026-09-06. (7) `BY EVERY t` as a spelling for a set-valued breach: not ruled, not built. CROSS-TRACK, not EVERY's: BPMN blame-set fidelity note (lts-diagrams); state-layer LEST re-looks marked Reoffered at the hand-off, O1/O2 (lts-diagrams-2, after #401).

decisions.ask: The weekly worktree prune never reaches /Volumes/transcend/src/l4wt, and 41 trees live there tonight after lts-diagrams-2 moved 14 idle ones to free the native disk (98% → 23% used). GM's recommendation: add the second glob, but (1) `git worktree lock --reason 'removable volume'` every transcend tree so `git worktree prune` cannot drop their admin entries while the volume is unmounted, and (2) have the job skip the transcend glob when the mount is absent. Also: trees created under the `legalese` login fail with 'dubious ownership' once moved (git checks the owner of .git/worktrees/<name>); mengwong has `safe.directory '/Volumes/transcend/src/l4wt/*'` now, the legalese login would need its own entry. The change lives in the homelab repo — session homelab-fc is idle if you want it done there.

decisions.ask: One bench of rulings the wave's tracks marked 'open to Meng' (every-each's words, outbox/20260916T212814Z-every-residue-after-wave.md): §5.2 (a) maximumStalledReoffers = 1000 as the stalled-chain bound; (b) a LEST under an anchored deadline already past at arming counts from a deadline EARLIER than the failed obligation's own entry — a max(deadline, arming) floor proposed, not applied; (c) a kept SHANT's HENCE clock is NOT moved (stays the revealing stamp) — §3.4 gives a reading under which it should. §5.1.1.1: an anchored ONCE-line deadline already past at the arming sends an EMPTY cast to the LEST, not the HENCE — chosen, marked open. 'May an empty cast be silent?' — a barrier over nobody fires its continuation on a vacuous join ('once all tenants have signed, the landlord must deliver' delivers when there are no tenants) while a fork over nobody fulfils; options: silent (today) / a run-time note through the notes channel / refuse the barrier over an empty cast / §10.3's static 'might be empty' warning. AFTER/BEFORE: the service notes schema; the text-dedup key for notes; a negative AFTER offset. Ledger, measured not decided: a RECORD inside a LEST continuation is stamped with the ROOT evaluation clock, never the contract clock. Say the word and GM sets these up as a cards page like the APPLIES bench; otherwise mark them here.
